problem: Most VLN-CE agents (including world-model ones such as DreamWalker and NavMorph) run open-loop at inference: they act without validating consequences, so latent-state drift and early errors accumulate. External feedback is sparse and delayed, and RL/MPC or entropy-based TTA signals are hard to train or decoupled from the agent's internal representation.
motivation: Navigation failures often come from gradual drift in the agent's internal understanding, not a single bad observation. Inspired by predictive processing, the paper asks whether an agent can derive an internal feedback signal from its own foresight to detect and correct this drift before acting.
key_idea: Use the latent discrepancy between a world model's foresight state and the current state as an internal feedback signal to refine the latent state before action selection, and trigger test-time world-model updates when this feedback strongly changes the action distribution.
insight: The ablation shows state-level refinement alone raises R2R-CE val-unseen SR from 43.77 to 48.34 and cuts TL from 26.16 to 21.75; VCM memory and feedback-triggered test-time adaptation (SR 50.90) add further gains. Feedback-triggered adaptation beats fixed-interval updates (SR 50.30 vs 50.90), and the foresight-reconstruction loss beats self-entropy and async scoring losses for TTA (SR 50.90 vs 49.48 and 50.19). Removing L_rec at training lowers SR to 48.89, so grounded foresight supervision is what makes the feedback informative.
method: Latent world model: recurrent latent state s_t with a posterior update q from the previous refined state, action, calibrated visual features and instruction, plus a Transformer prior transition f_p that predicts the foresight state without new observations.
Internal feedback: a foresight policy proposes a provisional action, the deterministic prior gives s~_{t+1}, and Delta_t = s~_{t+1} - s_t serves as guidance (not a loss target).
Feedback-guided plan refinement: a lightweight gated residual network psi(s_t, Delta_t) produces the refined state s_t^(Delta), from which the final navigation policy picks the action.

Visual Calibration Module (VCM): episodic memory of the last L=4 steps, cross-attended with a learnable temporal decay bias, relative 7-D geometric and step embeddings, and adaptive-gated fusion with current features.
Pre-training objective: L = L_ac (imitation on both s_t and s_t^(Delta)) + L_wm (KL between posterior and prior) + L_rec (MSE between decoded foresight and the next-step ViT visual feature).

Conditional world-aware adaptation: compute kappa_t = KL(p~_t || p_t) between the action distributions before and after refinement. If kappa_t exceeds the running tau=0.5 percentile and entropy of p_t is below a threshold, take a gradient step on L_rec updating only the world-model parameters (policies excluded).
Plug-in design: applied on VLN-3DFF (monocular) and on ETPNav and HNR (panoramic).

setting.backbone: Lightweight VLN-CE models (VLN-3DFF / ETPNav / HNR) with a Transformer world model; CLIP ViT-B/16 (R2R-CE) or ViT-B/32 (RxR-CE), ResNet-50 depth encoder, trained and fine-tuned
setting.training_data: R2R-CE / RxR-CE training data with expert-action imitation; R2R-CE initialized from R2R-CE-pretrained weights (25k iters), then 12k + 10k episodes; RxR-CE initialized from the VLN-3DFF checkpoint, 14k episodes; <40 GPU hours on one RTX 3090; test-time self-supervised adaptation
setting.observation: Monocular RGB-D (VLN-3DFF setting) or panoramic 12-view RGB-D at 30° intervals, plus instruction
setting.action_space: Predicted candidate waypoints on a topological graph, executed with low-level continuous control
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE) plus a real Unitree GO2 robot

results: SC2-WM improves every base model it is plugged into. Monocular on R2R-CE val-unseen, SR rises from 43.8 to 50.9 and SPL from 29.4 to 37.2 over the reproduced VLN-3DFF, with much shorter trajectories. Panoramic on HNR reaches SR 66 / SPL 54 on R2R-CE val-unseen (HNR* 61/51) and SR 60 / SPL 50 on RxR-CE val-unseen (HNR* 56/47). In the real-world test with a GO2 robot, SR is 85% vs 70% for the baseline.
limitations: Feedback quality depends on world-model expressiveness. Stronger 3DGS-based monoVLN and large MLLM-based methods (e.g. DualVLN, SR 64.3) still outperform the monocular variant on R2R-CE.
Test-time adaptation adds computation (about 17.78s to 18.92s per episode) and needs gradient updates on the robot, which are handled by offboard compute and asynchronous updates.
'Closed-loop' is really an internal latent refinement loop, not a true external feedback loop, and gains are modest on some metrics (e.g. R2R-CE panoramic on ETPNav, +2 SR).
